title: Flat modules remain flat at normalized stalks
statement: Let C be a category essentially small in the coefficient universe, J a Grothendieck topology, R a sheaf of commutative rings, p a point of Sh(C,J), and s a normalized ringed-site point [def-sfb-ringed-site-point], with stalk ring A and module functor S. If M is a flat sheaf of R-modules, then S(M) is a flat A-module.

source.place: Tag 05VD; geometric inverse image preserves flatness

proof.text: Use the singleton-site point presentation and its explicit tensor-compatible evaluation equivalence.

Apply algebraic inverse-image flatness with independent universes. The tensor functor with the image module is exact. Transport this through the tensor-compatible evaluation equivalence; the categorical exact-tensor criterion is ordinary module flatness.
